_auth_decision.how: Credentials live on `User` (email/encrypted_password); the n:1 FK runs User.account_id -> Account.id, opposite to the runtime's forward-only account_link. So ids are seeded aligned (User.id == Account.id) and session.account_id (fed from User.account_id via session_fields) equals Account.id, which is what every owner_col (`account_id`) and admin guard compares against. sign_in verifies against User; admin gating walks User.role_id -> UserRole.permissions via a two-hop grammar precondition.
_auth_decision.why_not_account_link: account_link resolves Account.id only when the link column lives on Account; here it lives on User (User.account_id), so account_link would resolve to User.id. Aligned ids are the faithful model.
